narrationScript:
Welcome to Chapter 1.2: Performance Metrics and the Iron Law. In this lesson, we will dive into the core principles that govern processor performance. Understanding these metrics is crucial for anyone designing, optimizing, or even just evaluating computer systems.

Our primary goal is to equip you with the tools to quantitatively analyze and compare different computer architectures. By the end of this chapter, you will be able to apply the Iron Law to calculate the execution time for a given program and processor. You'll learn to compute Cycles Per Instruction, or CPI, Instructions Per Cycle, IPC, and MIPS, from processor specifications and workload data.

We will also explore the critical relationship between clock frequency, pipeline depth, and overall performance, understanding how these factors interact. Finally, you will learn to use industry-standard benchmark suites, such as SPEC, Geekbench, and MLPerf, to effectively evaluate and compare processor performance in real-world scenarios. Let's begin our exploration into the heart of computer architecture performance.
